name: Incline Dumbbell Front Raise
description: The incline dumbbell front raise is performed lying face-down on an incline bench set to 45-60 degrees, raising dumbbells from the hanging position to shoulder height in front of the body. The incline position eliminates torso momentum and places the anterior deltoid under a greater stretch at the start of the movement. This improved bottom-position stretch and strict form requirement make it more effective as a pure anterior deltoid isolation exercise than the standing version.

execution.starting_position: Set an adjustable bench to 45-60 degrees. Lie face-down on the bench with the chest on the pad. Hold dumbbells with an overhand or neutral grip, arms hanging below the bench.
execution.setup_instructions: Use lighter weight than standing front raises. The hanging position creates a pre-stretch on the anterior deltoid.
steps: Step 1: Lie face-down on the incline bench, dumbbells hanging below.
Step 2: Begin from the full hang (arms straight down) for a maximum anterior deltoid stretch.
Step 3: Raise both dumbbells forward and upward in an arc.
Step 4: Raise until the arms are parallel to the floor.
Step 5: Lower slowly under full control to the hanging position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the raise, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Not using the full hang at the bottom, missing the stretch
Raising the head to look forward, which strains the neck
safety_considerations: Keep the head in a neutral position resting on the bench pad
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full hanging position to shoulder height (parallel to the floor).
coaching_cues: Raise forward — not to the side
Slow and controlled — this is not a strength exercise
